title: Why you lurch forward when a car brakes hard
examples: Why do I jerk forward when the car stops?
Why do seatbelts go across the hips and chest?

explain.say: When a car travels at 50 kilometres per hour, so do you. Your weight is balanced by the seat pushing up, so you sit still compared with the car.

explain.say: When the car brakes hard, the brakes slow the car, but only weak friction from the seat acts on you. Your body carries on forward at nearly its old speed, which is called inertia, so you lurch forward.

explain.say: A seatbelt gives a strong backward force across your hips and chest, the strong bony parts of the body. It slows you down along with the car instead of letting you hit the dashboard or windscreen.

forces.label: Seatbelt pull

forces.ask: How strong is the force on you in a crash?

explain.say: In a crash the force needed to stop you can be many times your weight. Belts are made to stretch slightly, which spreads the stopping over a little more time and makes that force smaller.

faq.q: What does a seatbelt do in a crash?
faq.a: A seatbelt pulls back on your hips and chest so you slow down with the car instead of carrying on forward into the dashboard, windscreen or other people.

faq.q: How strong is the force on you in a crash?
faq.a: Stopping from 50 kilometres per hour in a fraction of a second can need a force more than ten times your weight. That is why an unbelted person cannot brace themselves with their arms.
asks: Can you hold yourself back in a crash?

faq.q: Why do I feel pushed into my seat when a car speeds up?
faq.a: The seat has to push you forward to speed you up with the car. You feel that push on your back, even though nothing is pushing you backwards.
asks: Why do I sink into the seat when we accelerate?

faq.a: Inertia is the way an object keeps doing what it is doing, staying still or moving at a steady speed in a straight line, unless a force changes it. It is Newton's first law.
asks: Why do I keep moving when the car stops?
Why is seat friction not enough?

faq.q: Why do seatbelts cross the hips and chest?
faq.a: The pelvis and ribcage are strong bones that can take a big force. The belt spreads the force across them instead of the soft belly or the neck.

facts: Newton's first law says an object keeps moving at a steady speed in a straight line unless a force acts on it.
US road safety figures show lap-and-shoulder belts cut the risk of death for front-seat car occupants by about 45 percent.
Seatbelts stretch slightly in a crash, spreading the stopping over a little more time.

quiz.say: Why do passengers lurch forward when a car brakes suddenly?
quiz.show: Why do passengers lurch forward when a car brakes suddenly?

options.show: Their bodies keep moving forward because of inertia
options.say: Their bodies keep moving forward because of inertia

quiz.why: The brakes slow the car, but nothing strong slows your body at first, so it carries on forward.

wrong.1: Nothing pushes you forward; you simply keep moving while the car slows.
wrong.2: Moving air is not what throws passengers forward.
